Definition of risk (effect of uncertainty on objectives) — the composed concept.
Definition of control as measure modifying risk — distinguishes control from the other terms.
Alternative/current definition of control (measure that maintains and/or modifies risk).
Narrative on selecting and implementing controls to modify identified risks.
Explains information as an asset that has value and requires protection.
Explains information security concepts underpinning the vocabulary.

Definition of information security event — the lower threshold term the task contrasts.
Definition of information security incident — single or series of events that compromise operations/security.

Requires reporting of observed or suspected events, showing events are reported before classification.
Annex A control on assessment and decision on information security events (event-to-incident threshold).

dropped.why: Defines the incident-management process set, not the event/incident/breach thresholds.
Guidance on responding to incidents; says nothing about distinguishing events, incidents or breaches.
Planning/preparation guidance on roles and processes, not definitional thresholds.
PII privacy compliance guidance; no treatment of breach as an escalation term.

Prompts and inference inputs/outputs are information requiring classification, supporting 'prompt as data'.
Application security requirements are the anchor for treating an AI system as an application with new security requirements.
Secure architecture and engineering principles underpin the notion of the inference boundary / trust boundary.
Threat intelligence is how changes in the threat/attack surface from new technology are tracked.
AI capability is typically consumed as a cloud service; exposure of data to an external service boundary.
Supports the ability point: AI adoption is a change to be managed, not a procurement event.
Information security in project management - security considered when AI projects are initiated.
Data leakage prevention speaks to prompt content leaving the organisation's boundary.
New AI exposure must be identified and analysed through the information security risk assessment.
Operational planning and control covers planned changes such as introducing AI systems.
Definition of vulnerability underpins any 'attack surface' explanation.

Generic checklist of secure development lifecycle practices; says nothing about new technology exposure or attack surface.

results.statement: Distinguish model-level risks from agentic risks.
results.note: Agentic vs model-level AI risk, delegated authority and autonomy/blast radius are course-specific AI-security teaching material; ISO/IEC 27001/27002/27000/17021-1 contain no passage addressing AI models or agentic systems, so no clause can carry the key.

results.statement: Classify a described AI-related security concern against the appropriate threat category.
results.note: The AI threat taxonomy assessed here (training data poisoning, prompt injection, insecure output handling, tool misuse) comes from OWASP LLM Top 10 / AI-specific guidance, not from ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27000 or 17021-1; none of the listed clauses define or enumerate AI threat categories (27000 3.74 defines 'threat' generically only).
